- Continue the existing HELIX Evolution Lab and add a DNA sequence analyser.
- Make organisms develop visible biological systems—such as muscle, bones, neurons, fat, nerves, and ears—based on their DNA.

- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

- Treat the existing HELIX evolutionary simulation as the intended game.

### Completed
- Previously verified the existing game’s core interactions and build; no game code changes were made at that time.

- Plan and implement DNA sequence analysis and DNA-driven organism tissues/body systems.
- Recent inspection found existing numeric genome genes and visual body construction, but no DNA analyser implementation.

1. Define a DNA-sequence representation and analyser that fits the existing genome and mutation/breeding mechanics.

- Existing genome genes are normalized numeric alleles (`bodySize`, `neck`, `legs`, `tail`, `armor`, `speed`, `fat`, `crest`, `hue`, `pattern`); there is not yet a sequence analyser or explicit genes for muscle, bones, neurons, nerves, or ears.

- Extend the existing HELIX Evolution Lab with DNA sequence analysis and DNA-driven visible biological systems in organisms.

- Retain the existing simulation design and mechanics.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

### Completed

- Inspected the genome, creature construction, specimen UI, and DNA bank integration points.

## Objective
- Extend the HELIX Evolution Lab with DNA sequence analysis and DNA-driven visible biological systems while retaining its existing simulation design and mechanics.

## Requirements
- Keep DNA analysis compatible with the existing numeric genome; do not change genes or breeding mechanics.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Save screenshot checks as JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Encode each normalized gene allele as one byte represented by four two-bit DNA bases.
- Derive visible body systems from existing genes rather than adding genes.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `src/dna.js` with genome encoding, GC-content analysis, and derived expression values for muscle, bones, neurons, fat, nerves, and ears.
- Connected derived expression to visible body features in `src/creature.js`, including ears, muscles, bones, adipose, and neural structures.
- Added a DNA analyser to the specimen dossier in `index.html`, styled it in `src/style.css`, and wired selected-genome updates through `analyzeGenome` in `src/main.js`.
- Production build succeeded using `npm run build -- --outDir /tmp/opencode/helix-build`.

### Active
- Review body-system visuals and verify analyser behavior and visuals in a browser.
- Capture and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review the DNA-driven visuals in `src/creature.js` for any remaining expression gaps.
2. Run browser checks for selection updates and analyser presentation; capture a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.
3. Check final working-tree changes and report assumptions briefly.

## Relevant Files
- `src/dna.js`: Genome encoding, GC analysis, and derived system expression.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature construction and DNA-driven body visuals.
- `src/main.js`: Analyser rendering and selected-specimen updates.
- `index.html`: Dossier markup for the DNA analyser.
- `src/style.css`: Analyser styling and dossier layout.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. Earlier working-tree status showed modified `src/creature.js`, untracked `src/dna.js`, and generated `dist` changes; analyser changes were made afterward.
- The latest build emitted a non-blocking warning that the JavaScript bundle exceeds 500 kB.

## Objective
- Extend the HELIX Evolution Lab with DNA sequence analysis and DNA-driven visible biological systems while retaining its existing simulation design and mechanics.

## Requirements
- Keep DNA analysis compatible with the existing numeric genome; do not change genes or breeding mechanics.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Save screenshot checks as JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Encode each normalized gene allele as one byte represented by four two-bit DNA bases.
- Derive visible body systems from existing genes rather than adding genes.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `src/dna.js` with genome encoding, GC-content analysis, and derived expression values for muscle, bones, neurons, fat, nerves, and ears.
- Connected derived expression to visible body features in `src/creature.js`, including ears, muscles, bones, adipose, and neural structures.
- Added a DNA analyser to the specimen dossier in `index.html`, styled it in `src/style.css`, and wired selected-genome updates through `analyzeGenome` in `src/main.js`.
- Production build succeeded using `npm run build -- --outDir /tmp/opencode/helix-build`.
- Browser check confirmed 40 bp, 10 gene rows, six derived systems, and analyser content updating when selecting another specimen.

### Active
- Capture and inspect a fresh compliant JPEG screenshot; the CDP screenshot attempt timed out, so `/tmp/opencode/helix-latest.jpg` was not created.

### Blocked
- Screenshot capture through the current Chromium CDP session is timing out; a separate Chromium process also showed extreme GPU process CPU use.

## Next Move
1. Capture a fresh screenshot at 1280px wide or less, save as JPEG, and inspect only that newest screenshot.
2. Run a final build/status check and review generated `dist` changes.
3. Report the completed work and briefly note the assumption that each numeric allele is normalized and byte-encoded.

## Relevant Files
- `src/dna.js`: Genome encoding, GC analysis, and derived system expression.
- `src/creature.js`: Creature construction and DNA-driven body visuals.
- `src/main.js`: Analyser rendering and selected-specimen updates.
- `index.html`: Dossier markup for the DNA analyser.
- `src/style.css`: Analyser styling and dossier layout.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. `dist` has tracked generated-file deletions/modifications and new generated assets.
- Earlier screenshot `/tmp/opencode/helix-check.jpg` is stale and must not be inspected; capture a new one.
- The production build warning about JavaScript bundle size exceeding 500 kB is non-blocking.
